report.source_text: The patient was started on a 3 day course of pulsed methylprednisolone 1 g once daily, followed by a weaning course of oral prednisolone starting at 60 mg once daily. The patient then underwent 5 sessions of plasma exchange. Azathioprine was commenced at a dose of 25 mg once daily (TPMT 22), with the intention of uptitrating this to a maintenance dose of 75 mg once daily (∼1 mg / kg). Gabapentin 300 mg TDS was given to help treat the nystagmus.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 31-year-old woman presented with a one-month history of intractable hiccups, vomiting, unsteadiness, visual blurring, and mild headache. Neurological examination revealed horizontal torsional nystagmus, left upper limb dysmetria, and ataxic gait. MRI of the brain showed subtle FLAIR hyperintensity in the right superior cerebellar peduncle and periaqueductal grey matter, which progressed to involve the area postrema. Serum Aquaporin-4 antibodies were confirmed positive. Lumbar puncture was unremarkable. The patient was treated with pulsed methylprednisolone, plasma exchange, and azathioprine, leading to significant improvement in hiccups, nausea, and vomiting, though unsteadiness persisted at discharge after a one-month inpatient stay.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Patient presented with intractable hiccups and vomiting, unsteadiness, visual blurring, and mild headache.
Neurological examination showed horizontal torsional nystagmus, left upper limb dysmetria, and ataxic gait.

MRI brain revealed subtle FLAIR hyperintensity in the right superior cerebellar peduncle and periaqueductal grey matter, progressing to involve the area postrema, providing a structural correlate for hiccups, nausea, and vomiting.
Serum Aquaporin-4 antibodies were confirmed positive.
Treatment with pulsed methylprednisolone, plasma exchange, and azathioprine led to significant improvement in hiccups, nausea, and vomiting.

ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.basis: Unremarkable lumbar puncture (E002) and positive Aquaporin-4 antibodies (E005) make MS less likely.
While MOG-IgG status was not reported, the confirmed presence of Aquaporin-4 antibodies (E005) strongly points to AQP4-IgG positive NMOSD rather than MOGAD.

remaining_uncertainties: Detailed ophthalmological examination findings for optic neuritis, despite reported visual blurring.
MRI findings specifically for optic nerves or spinal cord (transverse myelitis).
Myelin Oligodendrocyte Glycoprotein (MOG-IgG) antibody test result.
Long-term clinical outcome beyond hospital discharge.
